title: Hosted API: Endpoint Stability, Compatibility and Migration PRD + Launch Checklist
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Purpose: Define the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and an operational launch checklist for shipping a compatibility-first rollout of the core hosted endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). This PRD covers API contract compatibility, SDK contract tests, client migration guidance, canary and rollback policies, monitoring/SLOs, and post-launch validation required to avoid regressions for existing customers.
goal: Ship backward-compatible endpoint surface with explicit deprecation and migration guidance while enabling safe canary rollouts that meet latency and correctness SLOs.
background: We are consolidating endpoint behavior and introducing a small set of contract clarifications (structured output hints, default sampling changes, and safety metadata). Historical customer feedback indicates regressions during previous surface changes caused client-side breakage. This effort focuses on minimizing regressions and giving customers a clear migration path.
scope_included: API contract compatibility tests for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
SDK contract test harness and CI gating
Migration docs, client opt-in flags, and deprecation window
scope_excluded: On-prem private deployment changes (handled by Private team)
New model architecture support beyond verified model catalog
key_user_stories: As an SDK user, I can run a compatibility test suite to ensure my integration doesn't break
As an SRE, I can pause and rollback a canary if error rate or latency thresholds are hit
As a PM, I can communicate deprecation dates and migration steps to customers
acceptance_criteria: All API contract changes are behind opt-in flags by default
SDKs (Python/TS/Go) pass the contract test suite in CI (no failing golden tests)
Canary passes defined stability criteria at 5% traffic for 72 hours before expansion
Per-endpoint percentiles: P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 400ms, error rate <= 0.25% for hosted tier
No functional correctness regressions on canonical prompt set (end-to-end evals show <= 1% metric drift vs baseline)
canary_criteria: Synthetic request success rate >= 99.75% over rolling 30m
No sustained CPU/GPU utilization rise > 15% above baseline without corresponding throughput increase
Model output regression checks: similarity metric on canonical prompts >= baseline-1% slack
No security scanner alerts or failing auth traces during canary period
rollback_plan: Immediate traffic kill switch at route level (console + API) in case of P95 latency > 600ms or error rate > 1%
Automated fallback to previous model variant for affected customers
Ticketing runbook: create INCIDENT-CANARY, notify on-call + PM + ENG leads, document postmortem within 48h
monitoring_slos: Availability SLO: 99.9% per route per week
Quality SLOs: end-to-end eval drift < 1% weekly aggregate on critical prompt set
qa_plan: Contract tests: run SDK contract suite against staging and canary clusters
Regression evals: run canonical prompt suite (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) nightly and compare to baseline
Chaos tests: simulate node preemption and partial KV cache cold start
Manual exploratory QA: safety prompts, structured output edge cases
rollout_checklist: 1) Merge SDK compatibility PRs and tag release candidates
2) Deploy runtime changes to staging with feature flags enabled
3) Run full contract test suite and nightly regression evals for 48h
4) Launch internal canary to 0.5% with telemetry collection enabled
5) Observe canary for 24h, then expand to 5% for 72h if all criteria pass
6) Open customer beta by invite with explicit opt-in flag and migration guide
7) Expand to 25% for 48h and monitor billing/latency metrics
8) After sustained success, promote to 100% and remove opt-in after deprecation window begins
9) Post-launch health review at 7 days and 30 days with documented metrics and learnings
api_contract_changes_summary: Clarify default sampling (temperature) contract: internal default changes should not alter behavior for customers who set explicit temperature
Add stable field names for structured outputs with backward-compatible aliases
client_migration_guidance: Provide example diff patches for Python/TS SDK usage
Offer automated CLI tool to run compatibility checks against a customer's test harness
Communications: send targeted emails to customers with >10k monthly requests and open support ticket for enterprise customers
security_and_compliance: KMS usage unchanged; ensure feature flags do not expose secrets
Run security review prior to 5% canary expansion
Privacy: embeddings outputs must not include latent identifiers; run embedding fingerprinting check
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: require opt-in feature flags for any output schema changes to avoid breaking existing clients
Tradeoff: slower default rollout cadence to reduce regression risk at cost of delaying feature availability
Decision: tighten P95 latency targets for chat endpoints; will increase infra cost temporarily
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff complete; initial impact mapping for top 50 customers
2025-02-20: SDK contract harness prototype merged to SDK monorepo; awaiting CI flakiness fixes
2025-02-28: Staging deployment passed unit/contract tests; nightly regressions running
2025-03-02: Security review scheduled for 2025-03-04; canary schedule proposed to SRE
risks: Risk: latent model output drift not captured by canonical prompt set; mitigation: expand prompt set and add human-in-the-loop review
Risk: SDK clients with pinned internal types may break; mitigation: provide aliasing shim and migration scripts
next_steps: Finalise canary playbook with SRE and on-call runbook
Complete security review and remediate findings
Publish migration docs and release SDK RCs before opt-in canary
notes: Keep stakeholders notified at each traffic expansion step
If any enterprise customer flags migration issues, pause expansion and remediate within 72h
